what: Eye candy: a screen on the wall of slowly flowing, glowing colour, like a lava lamp that your patch stirs.
how: The picture is a drifting mix of waves. Three signals (RED, GREEN and BLUE inputs) each push a different part of the picture around: a louder signal changes its pattern and makes the whole screen brighter. It makes no sound itself; the OUT is only all three inputs added together, so you can pass signals through. It shows its picture even when nothing downstream is heard.

ins.red: A signal that stirs the picture (audio or control).
ins.green: A second signal that stirs the picture.
ins.blue: A third signal that stirs the picture.

knobs.flow: How fast the picture drifts when nothing is patched.
knobs.hue: The base colour of the picture, turning round the colour wheel.

try: Patch a kick drum into RED, an LFO (a slow wobble) into GREEN and a hi-hat into BLUE. The colours then pulse with the beat and swirl with the LFO.
